grammar.title: There Is and There Are
grammar.explanation:
We use **there is** and **there are** to say that something is in a place.

Use **there is** with one thing. *There's a basin in my bathroom.* Use **there are** with many things. *There are two bedrooms in my house.*

For no, use **there isn't** and **there aren't**. *There isn't a basement in my flat. There aren't any boxes in the bedroom.*

For questions, use **Is there** and **Are there**. *Is there an armchair in your room? Are there any towels in the bathroom?*

In the past, use **there was** and **there were**. *There was a party at my house. There were many people.*
examples: *There's** a supermarket at the end of the street. (one thing)
*There are** twenty students in my class. (many things)
*There isn't** a lift in this building. (no)
*Are there** any good restaurants in your town? (question)
*There's** a soft armchair in my bedroom. (one thing)
*There are** two bathrooms in our house. (many things)

practice.q: Rewrite with **there is**: Our living room has a soft armchair.
practice.a: There is a soft armchair in our living room.

practice.q: Rewrite with **there are**: My flat has two bathrooms.
practice.a: There are two bathrooms in my flat.

practice.q: Make it negative: There is a basin in the bathroom.
practice.a: There isn't a basin in the bathroom.

practice.q: Make a question: There are boxes in the basement.
practice.a: Are there any boxes in the basement?
